Sternoclavicular injury: 5

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

CT confirms posterior sternoclavicular dislocation near major vessels. The patient needs reduction, but uncontrolled manipulation could disrupt adjacent structures. Which treatment setting and approach best reflect the special risk posed by this injury?

  1. Medial clavicular physeal injury
  2. CT assessment of the SC region
  3. Urgent reduction with appropriate specialist support
  4. Anterior medial-clavicle displacement
  5. Posterior medial-clavicle displacement
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Urgent reduction with appropriate specialist support

Posterior SC dislocation requires a controlled setting because manipulation can endanger adjacent major vessels.

Understanding the options

Urgent reduction with appropriate specialist support
Posterior SC dislocation requires a controlled setting because manipulation can endanger adjacent major vessels.
Anterior medial-clavicle displacement
Anterior SC dislocation commonly produces a palpable prominence over the joint. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Posterior medial-clavicle displacement
Posterior displacement can compress the trachea, esophagus and major vessels. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Medial clavicular physeal injury
The late-closing medial clavicular physis can mimic SC dislocation in young patients. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
CT assessment of the SC region
Plain radiographs can be difficult to interpret; CT defines SC displacement and adjacent anatomy. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
